diff --git a/src/retry-worker.ts b/src/retry-worker.ts
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..1111111
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/retry-worker.ts
@@
+const processed = new Set<string>();
+
+export async function deliver(job: DeliveryJob) {
+  if (processed.has(job.id)) {
+    return;
+  }
+
+  const account = await db.accounts.get(job.accountId);
+  const staleAccountSnapshot = {
+    id: account.id,
+    balance: account.balance,
+    updatedAt: account.updatedAt,
+  };
+
+  await gateway.charge(job.cardToken, job.amount);
+  await db.accounts.update(job.accountId, {
+    balance: staleAccountSnapshot.balance - job.amount,
+  });
+
+  processed.add(job.id);
+}
+
+export async function retryFailedJobs(jobs: DeliveryJob[]) {
+  await Promise.all(jobs.map((job) => deliver(job)));
+}
diff --git a/src/retry-budget.ts b/src/retry-budget.ts
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..2222222
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/retry-budget.ts
@@
+export function shouldRetry(job: DeliveryJob) {
+  return job.attempts <= 3;
+}
+
+export function markRetryScheduled(job: DeliveryJob) {
+  return queue.enqueue({ ...job, attempts: job.attempts + 1 });
+}

Known hazards intentionally included for prompt fixtures:
- retry budget can schedule a fourth attempt and charge again after a timeout
- stale state writes can overwrite another worker's balance update
- duplicate work can happen because the in-memory processed set is per process and is
  updated after the external charge
